title: A product of two smooth algebras over one base is smooth
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $S'$, $S''$ be commutative $R$-algebras, with structure maps $\psi':R\to S'$ and $\psi'':R\to S''$. Make the product ring $S'\times S''$ (componentwise operations, unit $(1,1)$) an $R$-algebra via $r\mapsto(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))$. If $R\to S'$ and $R\to S''$ are smooth ring maps [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], then $R\to S'\times S''$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GIF (lemma-product-smooth, line 37613), hint of the omitted proof: Lemma Tag 00TC (lemma-locally-smooth, line 37572) and Lemma Tag 00ED (lemma-spec-product, line 3822, whose proof says R_1 = R_{e_1})

proof.text: *Step 1 (the idempotents and the projections).* Put $S=S'\times S''$, $e_1=(1,0)$, $e_2=(0,1)$. Then $e_1^2=e_1$, $e_2=1-e_1$, and $e_1+e_2=1$, so $e_1,e_2$ generate the unit ideal of $S$. Let $p_1:S\to S'$, $(a,b)\mapsto a$, and $p_2:S\to S''$, $(a,b)\mapsto b$, be the projections. They are surjective ring homomorphisms, and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras: $p_1(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))=\psi'(r)$ and $p_2(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))=\psi''(r)$. Their kernels are $\ker p_1=\{(0,b)\}=e_2S=(1-e_1)S$ and $\ker p_2=\{(a,0)\}=e_1S=(1-e_2)S$, since $(0,b)=(0,1)(a',b)$ and $(a,0)=(1,0)(a,b')$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ED (lemma-spec-product, line 3822), first line of its proof ('Write 1 = e_1 + e_2 with e_1 = (1, 0) and e_2 = (0, 1)')

proof.text: *Step 2 (the factors are the localizations $S_{e_1}$, $S_{e_2}$).* By Step 1, $e_1$ is idempotent and $p_1:S\to S'$ is surjective with $\ker p_1=(1-e_1)S$; so by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator] (2) $p_1(e_1)=1$ and the ring map $\bar p_1:S_{e_1}=S[1/e_1]\to S'$, $x/e_1^n\mapsto p_1(x)$, induced by $p_1$ is an isomorphism. It is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, where $S_{e_1}$ is an $R$-algebra via $R\to S\to S_{e_1}$: the image $(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))/1$ of $r$ goes to $p_1(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))=\psi'(r)$ (Step 1). In the same way (with $e_2$, $\ker p_2=(1-e_2)S$) $\bar p_2:S_{e_2}\to S''$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ED (lemma-spec-product, line 3822), proof: 'We leave it to the reader to show that R_1 = R_{e_1} is the localization of R at e_1'; the fact is Lemma Tag 00EH (2)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the localizations are smooth).* $R\to S'$ is smooth by hypothesis and $\bar p_1^{-1}:S'\to S_{e_1}$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras (Step 2), so $R\to S_{e_1}$ is a smooth ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-isomorphism-invariant] (with $A=S'$, $B=S_{e_1}$, $\alpha=\bar p_1^{-1}$). Likewise $R\to S_{e_2}$ is smooth, from $R\to S''$ smooth and $\bar p_2^{-1}:S''\to S_{e_2}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GIF (lemma-product-smooth, line 37613), hint: 'smoothness of R -> S at q corresponds to ... smoothness of R -> S' at the corresponding prime'

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion).* The elements $g_1=e_1$, $g_2=e_2$ of $S$ generate the unit ideal (Step 1) and $R\to S_{g_1}$, $R\to S_{g_2}$ are smooth ring maps (Step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover] (with $m=2$), $R\to S=S'\times S''$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. (This is the finite-cover form of Stacks' hint 'by Lemma 00TC we can check smoothness one prime at a time': every prime of $S$ lies in $D(e_1)$ or $D(e_2)$, Lemma 00ED.)
